pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Mission and Vision Statements
pageCache.text:
Mission and Vision Statements
Facta non Verba
Our school moto reminds us that 'actions not words' guide us in all that we do.
The aims of the school are to foster the Christian traditions of the school and to maintain the ethos of caring and consideration for others.
Within the ethos of our Catholic and Christian community our Mission is to create:
a respectful community which values individuality and diversity;
a welcoming and caring school;
a school where pupils and staff feel happy, supported, safe and secure;
a learning community with a strong sense of Christian values, working in partnership with parents
A wealth of education and moral experiences
Motivation for each child and adult to achieve their full potential
Recognition of achievements both inside and outside school
Vision Statement
Our school undertook a series of visioning sessions involving pupils, parents and staff. During these meetings we discussed a variety of options for our core values and vision statement.Having reviewed all contributions, we agreed on the following vision statement, which we can all share and passionately embrace to help lead us forward as one unified yet diverse community.
Our school vision is to provide within a nurturing and respectful community, a diverse and inspirational learning experience delivered by skilled, passionate staff to motivated pupils. We aim to empower each child towards striving for excellence and fulfilling their full potential.
This vision will be best realised by fulfilling our school motto: facta non verba; actions not words.
Our Core Values
As a community, we have identified four core values that stem from our School Vision and are woven into the very fabric of the school. We expect all members of the school community - pupils, staff, trustees and clergy- to model these.
Our core values are:
C – Care
This connects us with each other and our community. “We who are many, are one body in Christ." (Romans 12:5)
O – Opportunity
This means utilising what is provided within our school community. “So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to those who are of the household of faith.” (Galatians 6:10).
R – Respect
This means regard highly, value, honour. "And as you wish that others would do to you, do so to them." (Luke 6:31)
E - Excellence
This means being outstanding or striving to reach your full potential. "Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart as working for the Lord." (Colossians 3:23-24).

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - PTA Welcome
pageCache.text:
PTA Welcome
Welcome to the PTA! We are an active group of parents and carers who run social and fundraising events to provide our children with some great opportunities and support our school community. Some great things we have funded in the past include a Christmas pantomime, new laptops for the school, playground equipment, musical instruments, educational virtual reality experiences for the children and more.
All members of the school community are automatically members of the PTA! This includes parents, grandparents, carers, the teaching staff, school management and office, and pupils.
What is our PTA all about?
We share a common goal, working together to strengthen our community and support the pupils of St Mary’s Hare Park School. We do this via range of child orientated and fundraising social events across the year. The PTA does this by:
supporting school events such as sports day
conducting fundraising events and more!
How is the PTA run?
The PTA is overseen by a board. This meets regularly and coordinates all PTA activities, which involves liaising with staff, parents and class representatives. There are regular PTA meetings for all to attend and events and activities you can get involved in.
We put all our news and events up on Classlist. It’s a free, safe, secure online community for us all where you can post questions and message other parents in your child’s class or year group. It’s really useful for tracking down lost jumpers, organising playdates, messaging parents, checking on homework and more!
To sign up and join our Classlist you can do so from here Join Classlist
Each class also has a class representative who liaises between the classes and the PTA, keep parents informed about fundraising events and asks for volunteers to help with those events.
How can I get involved?
Any help you can provide is very much appreciated, and in return you'll receive a huge sense of satisfaction and most likely a new group of friends. On top of that, there's a lot of evidence to suggest that when parents are engaged in a school, a child's attainment is improved; so could there be a more compelling reason to get involved?
Second Hand Uniform Sale
The PTA run an online second hand uniform shop which you can access through our PTA Classlist website. All items are in excellent condition, and lovingly laundered by the PTA. You can order anytime of the day or night and collect it from the school. It's a great way to re-use clothes , raise funds and help save the environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Catholic Social Teaching
pageCache.text:
Catholic Social Teaching
What is Catholic Social Teaching (CST)
Catholic social teaching (CST) is rooted in Scripture, formed by the wisdom of Church leaders, and influenced by grassroots movements. It is our moral compass, guiding us on how to live out our faith in the world.
How do we deliver the principles of Catholic Teaching at St Mary’s Hare Park?
Our faith calls us to love God and to love our neighbours in every situation, especially our sisters and brothers living in poverty. Following in the footsteps of Christ, we hope to make present in our unjust and broken world, the justice, love and peace of God. We have chosen 7 themes, with the help of CAFOD’s resources, to focus our understanding.
Human dignity means that everyone is special. We are each beautifully made in the image and likeness of God. Because everyone is special, we should treat every person the way we would like to be treated ourselves. God is present in every human person, regardless of religion, culture, nationality, orientation or economic standing. We are called to treat every person and every creature with loving respect.
Common good means that we are called to work for the good of each and all. What we do affects everyone and when we make choices we should think about how it affects others.
Peace is a cornerstone of our faith. Christ, the Prince of Peace, sacrificed himself with love on the cross. We see in our faith an opportunity to provide peace through our words, actions and prayer.
Help for the Poor & Vulnerable
This principle reminds us of God’s preferential love for the poorest and most vulnerable people. God’s love is universal; he does not side with oppressors, but loves the humble. We are called to protect and aid those in need.
Dignity of Workers and Participation
The Church teaches us that earning a fair living and having an equal voice that can be heard is essential in treating people with dignity. It is a call to put the human person above greed and profit.
Solidarity means that we show that we care for others. We can be better global neighbours by speaking out for justice and working actively for the good of all our sisters and brothers.
In the first pages of the Bible we read how God created the sun and the stars, the water and earth, and every creature. We believe Christ is the redeemer of all creation. The Earth is a gift from God and we are its protectors and custodians - caring for our world is to care for the gifts God has given us.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Head's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Head's Welcome
A very warm welcome to St. Mary’s Hare Park Catholic Independent School and Nursery.
The school was founded and established as a Charitable Trust under the management of the Board of Trustees to provide education for Roman Catholic children, however, the school has a rich, multi-cultural tradition and we welcome families of other denominations/religions who are willing to support the ethos of the school. Admission is for girls and boys from 2½ years to 11 years, from our Nursery through to Year 6.
St. Mary’s Hare Park is a place which is very special to everyone who comes here – be it as a child, parent or a member of staff. We are all very proud of our school and of the children’s learning and achievements. We provide a safe, caring and supportive atmosphere in which children can learn, play and enjoy. Our curriculum offers our pupils rich and exciting learning opportunities and inspires them to do their very best.
St. Mary's Hare Park School is known for its strong sense of community and values. We instill important values like respect, kindness, and responsibility in our students, fostering a positive and inclusive school culture.
We are motivated at St Marys Hare Park to provide the best learning environment for all our learners and endeavour to provide children with the confidence and drive to succeed at this early stage of their learning journeys.
Our catholic values guide us all in that we do and seek to achieve, and spreading the positive word of God to all within and beyond the school community.
We take our responsibility to provide an ‘education for life’ seriously and aim to prepare all of our students to meet their future with confidence.
Our small school comes with a big heart, and our children and staff are rightly very proud of our school and the warm community spirit that envelops us all. We believe that learning should be exciting, challenging and stimulating, allowing all our children to reach their full potential.
We would love to welcome you to experience the warm ethos, family feel and the high academic standards which are the key features of life at our wonderful school.
Ludovic Bernard - Head Teacher

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Drama/Lamda
pageCache.text:
Drama/Lamda
Dramatic activity is already a part of most children’s lives before they even start School. In the general form of ‘play’ this enables children to make sense of their own identity by exploring meaningful fictional situations that parallels the real world.
When Drama is both structured and fun, it encourages children to think and act creatively thus developing critical thinking and problem solving skills that can be applied to all areas of their learning. Drama gives children the opportunity to explore, experiment, create, perform and evaluate in a supportive and safe environment here at St Mary’s Hare Park School.
Our combined curriculum of both Drama and LAMDA examinations, aims to provide children with vital life skills that will serve them well throughout their education and beyond.
Participating in both Drama and LAMDA examinations, pupils will benefit from:
LAMDA examinations are taken in both Key Stage 1 and 2 and allow pupils the opportunity to gain Ofqual recognised qualifications in both Performance and Communication disciplines.
LAMDA qualifications are Ofqual regulated and have helped hundreds of thousands of candidates develop lifelong skills. LAMDA ignites the imagination, improves confidence with public speaking, develops the ability to memorise and recall information, expands vocabulary and improves speaking & listening skills.
As the need to succeed in Secondary School interviews, University applications and job interviews builds, LAMDA examinations will play a key role in developing pupils into confident and engaging communicators.
If pupils later decide to progress through the LAMDA grade system, the higher levels at Grade 6, 7 and 8 attract UCAS Points and can therefore, be extremely beneficial for both University applications, interviews and employment.
In Key Stage 1, pupils participate in the LAMDA Introductory examinations. These are a gentle step into the LAMDA suite of graded examinations. The syllabus enables appropriate development in interpretative skills, technical skills and communication skills.
At Key Stage 2, both Public Speaking and Acting examinations are taken. These exams are a great opportunity for children to develop essential communication skills that will aid Secondary School interviews and presentations.
Public speaking examinations develop skills for effective oral communication and public presentation. Pupils are required to select, structure and shape subject matter into a concise speech for an intended audience.
The LAMDA public speaking exam syllabus also teaches students study skills for memorising, which is easily transferable into other subject areas and can have considerable impact upon abilities to learn and revise. Therefore, ultimately helping to improve progress and attainment at School in many curriculum areas.
Solo Acting examinations are designed to develop the necessary skills to communicate a dramatic text to an audience. The syllabus offers learning objectives within interpretation, technical skill and knowledge.
LAMDA exams are about achievement, recognising and rewarding the endeavours of each individual. But they are also about empowerment. Designed to develop life skills in:
The Drama department ensures pupils are engaged and enthused in activities, performances and examinations that challenge and reward their individual efforts.
Where possible, the School will enter pupils in events that continue to encourage and develop their skills and talents.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Music forms a very important part of the curriculum and school life at St. Mary’s Hare Park School. Music is a unique way of communicating that can inspire and motivate children. It is a vehicle for personal expression and can play an important part in the personal development of children.
ISA Music Competition Winner
At St. Mary’s Hare Park, we aim to make music an enjoyable learning experience, encouraging the children to participate in a variety of musical experiences. Class lessons involve singing, learning to play musical instruments, understanding the language of music, listening, composing and performing. All of the children throughout the school participate in concert performances each year. This may involve both singing and playing musical instruments, either as a soloist or part of a musical ensemble
Musical instrument lessons take place in school during lunchtime or after the end of the normal school day. The school has a choir and orchestra which rehearse weekly. Each year the musical ensembles within the school take part in concerts, workshops, and activities in the wider community. In the past the school ensembles have participated in concerts at the Queen’s Theatre in Hornchurch, the Barbican Centre and Royal Albert Hall in London, and also performed at the National Finals of the Music for Youth Competition at the Royal Festival Hall in London and Symphony Hall in Birmingham. The school also arranges regular concert trips to London where the children can experience live music performed by professional musicians, most notably the London Symphony Orchestra, the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra, and the Royal Ballet at Covent Garden.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
The school curriculum is wide and varied and, whilst concentrating on the core areas of Literacy and Language Development, Mathematics, Science and Religious Education, it also includes Computing, Physical Education, Music, History, Geography, Design and Technology, Art and Craft, Lamda, Drama and French.
As part of the school's physical education programme, we provide the opportunity for children in Years 3 - 6 to attend regular swimming lessons at a local pool. They are taught to become competent and confident in water through the use of recognised strokes, personal survival skills and distance challenges. Over recent years we have purchased a number of bicycles and balance bikes to enable cycling to be incorporated into our physical education timetable.
The school participates in numerous activities and sporting events as a member of the Havering Sports Collective. Having recently become a member of the Independent School's Association, we look forward to wealth of sporting, music and art opportunities for children of all ages, competing against other prestigious independent schools in the region and further afield.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
Special Educational Needs & Disability
St Mary's Hare Park School offers a caring and nurturing environment for all children, promoting academic excellence as well as providing an exciting and varied curriculum in order to foster a love of learning so that every child can achieve their full potential.
St Mary's Hare Park School Special Educational Needs and Disability policy details how we do our utmost to ensure that the necessary provision is made for any pupils who have Special Educational Needs and Disabilities.
We are committed to a policy of inclusion, equal opportunity and, where reasonable, follow best practice as outlined in the statutory guidelines on special education needs and disabilities, in particular the SEN and Disability Code of Practice: 0 to 25 years 2015 (SEND Code 2015) and the Children and Families Act 2014.
Ms Barr is our Acting SENDco with Support form Mrs Rafi.
You can contact us via email or by phoning the school office and leaving a message (01708 761220).
Local Offer
The Havering Local Offer is where you can find information online in one single place about the services and support available locally for children, young people and adults with special educational needs and disabilities.
The purpose of the Local Offer is to allow those with special educational needs or disabilities, and their families, to clearly see what help and services are available across the London Borough of Havering.
You can also see how to contact the services and what you should do if you think you or your child could benefit from them.
Covering education, health and social care for those aged from birth to 25 years, the Local Offer is being developed with children, young people, parents, carers and local services, including pre-schools, schools, colleges and health and social care agencies.
The Local Offer for Havering can be found here:
https://familyserviceshub.havering.gov.uk/

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Hare Park School and Nursery - Art
pageCache.text:
Art
Our art and design education aims to equip children with the skills to experiment, invent, and create while fostering cross-curricular links to enhance their learning. As they progress, pupils will develop critical thinking and a deeper understanding of art and design, connecting it to other subjects and encouraging a holistic approach to their education.
In Pre-Prep, children engage with the arts through play, building self-expression, vocabulary, and understanding, while exploring concepts in subjects like literacy, mathematics, and science. They experiment with colour, design, and media, reinforcing cross-curricular learning and laying the foundation for further artistic exploration.
In Lower Prep, children explore various art styles—such as pencil work, painting, sculpture, and collage—while making connections to history, science, and geography. They study famous artists and tie art to literacy through discussions and reflections, linking their creative work to the wider world around them.
In Upper Prep, children study significant artists, architects, and designers from different historical and contemporary periods. They expand their mastery of techniques like drawing, painting, and sculpture, drawing links between these practices and subjects like history, science, and technology. Sketchbooks help them refine ideas, while they learn to evaluate and analyse artwork using the language of art and design.
We are fortunate to have the opportunity to enter ISA competitions, which provide a platform for our students to showcase their artistic talents and creativity. These competitions allow children to demonstrate their skills across a variety of media, while also fostering collaboration, confidence, and a sense of achievement. By participating in these events, students represent the school and further their personal growth, reinforcing the cross-curricular connections they’ve made in their art and design learning and celebrating their artistic accomplishments.

Computing
At St Mary’s Hare Park School, Computing is about far more than using technology. Our curriculum equips pupils with the knowledge, skills and understanding to thrive in an increasingly digital world, whilst developing creativity, problem-solving, resilience and responsible digital citizenship.
Our Computing curriculum is built around three key strands:
Computer Science Pupils develop computational thinking through coding, algorithms, programming and problem-solving. From programming Bee-Bots in the Early Years to creating projects using Micro:bits and physical computing in Upper Prep, children learn how digital systems work and how technology can be designed to solve real-world problems.
Information Technology Pupils learn to use technology purposefully, creatively and effectively. Using a range of digital tools and platforms, children create, organise and present content, communicate ideas and collaborate with others. Technology is embedded across the curriculum, supporting learning in subjects such as English, Mathematics, Science, Art and Humanities.
Digital Literacy Online safety and digital citizenship underpin all aspects of Computing. Pupils are taught how to use technology safely, responsibly and respectfully, how to evaluate information critically and how to navigate the online world with confidence. They learn about privacy, digital footprints, misinformation and the responsible use of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI).
As a forward-thinking school, we also recognise the growing importance of Artificial Intelligence. In line with our AI Policy, pupils are introduced to age-appropriate AI concepts and learn to understand both the opportunities and limitations of AI-generated content. Staff use approved AI tools to enhance teaching and learning, while ensuring all use remains safe, ethical and compliant with safeguarding and data protection requirements.
Through a rich and engaging Computing curriculum, we aim to develop confident, creative and responsible digital learners who are well prepared for the next stage of their education and the rapidly evolving world beyond the classroom.

Pre-Prep (Early Years)
The children at St Mary’s Hare Park all bring their own individual experiences, skills and needs as they start school with us. We aim to value and build on this individuality and provide an environment where they are nurtured and cared for in their early year’s education.
The children attend our Nursery class (age from 2.5 years) for agreed sessions across the week and wear our nursery uniform.
They attend Pre-School class (from the September or January before they are 4 years old) or the Reception class (the September before they are 5 years old.) full time and wear our school uniform.
The children follow the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum which provides a nurturing start to their education covering all seven areas of their developmental learning.
In the final term of Reception class the children move towards a more structured approach to learning in readiness for their move into Key Stage 1.
